title: A spatial angular null numerator removes only one of the two near-parallel derivative losses

null_order_boundary.ray: Take p=(1,0,0), k=(K,1,0), omega=sqrt(M^2+|k|^2) and Phi=1+omega(k)-omega(k+p)
null_order_boundary.spatial_angular_numerator: |p cross k|=1 and the Coulomb-transverse numerator e dot (2k+p)=2 for e=(0,1,0)
null_order_boundary.spatial_order: The raw spatial-null quotient is Theta(K^2); after one matter-energy normalization by omega(k) it is still Theta(K), so first-order angular cancellation is not same-tier
null_order_boundary.lorentz_order: N0/Phi=(1+omega(k)+omega(k+p))/2=Theta(K), while N0/(omega(k)Phi) tends to 1 and is same-tier
null_order_boundary.structural_consequence: The missing extra cancellation is the time-space Lorentz combination, not ordinary spatial transversality or one angular null factor; a successful repair must recover that combination, add another cancellation, or use a different spacetime or modified-energy mechanism
null_order_boundary.ceiling: This ray classifies the declared first-order spatial and Lorentz numerators only; it is not a no-go for full-current decompositions, bilinear estimates, higher null structures, dispersive bounds or nonlinear modified energies
